Clinical details: Severe aortic stenosis with exertional syncope. Ex-smoker, 30 pack-years. TAVI work-up.

Technique: ECG-gated CT angiography of the aortic root and heart, followed by non-gated CT angiography from the thoracic inlet to the lesser trochanters. 80 ml iohexol 350. DLP 704 mGy·cm.

Findings:

Thoracic aorta: Ascending aorta 37 mm. Arch and descending thoracic aorta of normal calibre. No dissection. Moderate arch and descending aortic atheroma without mobile component.

Subclavian/axillary arteries: Unremarkable. No significant stenosis.

Abdominal aorta: Normal calibre. No abdominal aortic aneurysm. Coeliac axis, SMA and renal arteries patent.

Iliofemoral access (minimal luminal diameter):
Right: CIA 7.9 mm, EIA 6.8 mm, CFA 7.1 mm.
Left: CIA 8.2 mm, EIA 7.0 mm, CFA 7.4 mm.
Calcification: moderate, non-circumferential. Tortuosity: mild. No dissection or flow-limiting stenosis.

Lungs and airways: 6 mm solid nodule in the right upper lobe (series 5, image 88). No other pulmonary nodule. Mild centrilobular emphysema. No consolidation. Airways patent. Surveillance per BTS guidance is appropriate only if the patient would be fit for further investigation or treatment; for consideration by the referring team.

Pleura and pericardium: No pleural or pericardial effusion.

Mediastinum: No mediastinal or hilar lymphadenopathy.

Upper abdomen: Unremarkable within the limits of an arterial phase study.

Bones: No aggressive osseous lesion. Old healed left 7th rib fracture.

Conclusion:
1. Iliofemoral access favourable for a transfemoral approach bilaterally; minimal luminal diameter right 6.8 mm, left 7.0 mm.
2. 6 mm solid right upper lobe nodule; see surveillance comment above.

Annular sizing, valve morphology, coronary ostial heights and aortic root measurements are reported separately in the structural heart report; please refer to that report for valve planning.
